harbor.practice: Harbor's 4.2M documents become ≈ 38M chunks; at 768 dims in int8 that is ≈ 29 GB of vectors per replica before graph links and metadata.
harbor.failure: Treating raw vector bytes as total storage or RAM demand.

harbor.practice: A Harbor parser pod crashed after writing chunks but before acking; redelivery produced no duplicates because chunk IDs are deterministic and writes carry a version guard.
harbor.failure: Watching worker latency while the queue's oldest-message age grows: that is a freshness incident.

harbor.practice: Harbor's travel policy table (rows = regions, columns = per-day limits) is stored as structured rows; flattening it had caused wrong per-diem answers.
harbor.failure: Assuming a parse that produced lots of text was read correctly.

harbor.practice: Harbor's freshness SLO is "99% of edits searchable within 10 minutes; deletions within 5", measured per change from source timestamp to index timestamp.
harbor.failure: Deleting the source file and forgetting the vectors, caches and summaries derived from it.

harbor.practice: Harbor's three largest customers have dedicated shards; the other 1,197 share placement-by-hash shards, and a tenant is promoted when it passes 5M chunks or 50 QPS.
harbor.failure: Adding replicas to fix an ingestion bottleneck; replicas help reads, not writes.

harbor.practice: When an employee leaves Finance, Harbor's deny list blocks Finance documents for them immediately, before the next ACL sync updates the index.
harbor.failure: Filtering restricted documents after the model has already seen them.

harbor.practice: Harbor's index manifest binds embedder v2 to index v2; rollback switches both the alias and the query encoder together.
harbor.failure: Assuming equal vector dimensions make two embedding models compatible.

harbor.practice: Harbor's benchmark replays 2,000 logged queries with real ACL filters while 5% of the corpus is updated, and reports p95 latency and Recall@10 together.
harbor.failure: Benchmarking with repeated identical queries, which mostly measures the cache.

harbor.practice: Only 6% of Harbor queries were multi-hop; query decomposition fixed most of them, so a knowledge graph was deferred.
harbor.failure: Adopting an advanced retrieval technique because of its name, without a failure analysis showing the gap.
